These are PUBLIC SYNTHETIC test vectors. Never use their mnemonic or password
for funds. No real wallet or private user data was used.

The password is `Public Skull Island password: é雪!`. The mnemonic is the
English BIP39 all-zero 256-bit vector: `abandon` repeated 23 times, then `art`.
The ciphertext and password verifier were generated independently with Node's
built-in `crypto`, using the exact HMAC keys and AES slices in Skull Island's
writer; they were not generated by the Python recovery implementation.

`zero_wallet.json` uses the settings-only writer in:
https://github.com/PirateNetwork/Skull-Island/blob/c780b5f60ff8284b1d591631fab54dcfe97fd052/SaplingMobile/src/App.jsx#L369

`old_zero_wallet.json` uses the older top-level `secretPhrase` writer in:
https://github.com/PirateNetwork/Skull-Island/blob/c22833acd41cc08448a092def5474e11316ca3df/SaplingMobile/src/index.js#L19

The AES/HMAC code and fixed ASCII salts are identical in those source versions:
https://github.com/PirateNetwork/Skull-Island/blob/c780b5f60ff8284b1d591631fab54dcfe97fd052/SaplingMobile/src/utils/hash.js

Reproduce the public crypto fields using Node:

```javascript
const crypto = require('crypto');
const password = 'Public Skull Island password: é雪!';
const seed = Array(23).fill('abandon').join(' ') + ' art';
const pwSalt = 'b442d703357362b59017c9ea8823f6b8412bad33f1a6d8fec5e41a47689fd524';
const keySalt = '7b792df82bc433faa6913e3034d103f00c64360f081c7a88a8c8527652693dff';
const digest = crypto.createHmac('sha512', keySalt).update(password).digest('hex');
const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv('aes-256-cbc',
  Buffer.from(digest.slice(0, 64), 'hex'),
  Buffer.from(digest.slice(64, 96), 'hex'));
const passPhrase = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(seed), cipher.final()]).toString('hex');
const verifier = crypto.createHmac('sha512', pwSalt).update(password).digest('hex');
console.log({password: verifier, passPhrase});
```

Native tests build an in-memory key-prefix fixture, not a claim of a complete
native transaction database, following the pinned native writer. They use the
public Sapling keys generated by the SDK in `../native_sdk_keys.json`, separate
encrypted imported-key records, fixed public nonces and public entropy. The
Android writer transports Base64 but writes the *decoded raw bytes*:
https://github.com/PirateNetwork/cordova-plugin-litewallet/blob/e7c2412fa89a89a71a9e90b3ab007a56814b755d/native/android/litewallet-jni/src/com/rust/litewalletjni/LiteWalletJni.java

Its backend is PirateNetwork/piratewallet-light-cli commit
`9cc504db0f77406b13ad55c1df3b3cb4cb00cb36`; its key serialization files are
identical to the Lite parser's `83f96539411ab70775c22fc0252c4460c2189489`.

The explicit old Android password test uses the independently source-proven
literal `[]`, never a password search:
https://github.com/PirateNetwork/cordova-plugin-litewallet/blob/9bf9264e77b11926cf54160d1d07f8061d841b2b/www/litewallet.js#L45
https://github.com/PirateNetwork/cordova-plugin-litewallet/blob/9bf9264e77b11926cf54160d1d07f8061d841b2b/www/litewallet.js#L89
